body_text: Summer fatigue is common, but simple lifestyle changes can help you beat tiredness during hot weather When summer arrives, many people expect to feel happier, healthier, and more energetic. Longer days, warmer weather, holidays, and more time outdoors are often associated with feeling refreshed. However, many people experience the opposite. Instead of feeling energised, they feel unusually tired, sluggish, and drained. This phenomenon is often referred to as summer fatigue , and it can happen for several reasons. Changes in temperature, disrupted sleep patterns, dehydration, allergies, and increased alcohol consumption can all affect how well your body functions during the warmer months. Medical doctor and wellness expert explains that summer tiredness is not unusual. The body has to constantly adapt to environmental changes, and these adjustments can use energy. If you are wondering why you feel exhausted despite enjoying sunny weather, these five common causes may explain it. 1. Hot Weather Can Leave You Feeling Exhausted Heatwaves and rising summer temperatures can put extra stress on the body. Your body works hard to maintain a stable internal temperature, and when the weather becomes extremely warm, this process can affect your energy levels. The human body functions best within a narrow temperature range. When temperatures rise significantly, the body needs to use additional energy to cool itself down. This can leave you feeling tired, slow, and less focused. One way to reduce heat-related fatigue is to help your body cool down naturally. Cooling areas such as your palms, forehead, and the soles of your feet can help lower body temperature more effectively. Try using a cool, damp cloth on these areas or placing your feet in cool water. The goal is to cool the body gradually rather than using extremely cold temperatures, which can cause blood vessels to tighten and reduce the cooling effect. Other ways to manage heat fatigue include: Staying indoors during the hottest part of the day Wearing lightweight, breathable clothing Keeping your home cool and well ventilated Taking regular breaks when exercising outdoors 2. Dehydration Can Reduce Energy Levels One of the most common causes of summer tiredness is dehydration. Hot weather increases sweating, which means your body loses more fluid than usual. If you do not replace those fluids, even mild dehydration can affect your physical and mental performance. Many people wait until they feel thirsty before drinking water. However, thirst is actually a late warning sign that your body needs more fluids. Even mild dehydration can contribute to: Low energy Headaches Dizziness Difficulty concentrating Feeling generally unwell A simple way to monitor hydration is to check the colour of your urine. Pale yellow usually indicates good hydration, while darker shades may suggest that you need to drink more water. During hot weather, make a habit of drinking regularly throughout the day rather than relying only on thirst. If you are exercising, spending time outdoors, or sweating heavily, you may need additional fluids. 3. Alcohol Can Affect Summer Sleep Quality Summer often brings more social events, holidays, outdoor gatherings, and celebrations. As a result, some people drink alcohol more frequently during the warmer months. Although a drink may help you relax, alcohol can interfere with the quality of your sleep. You may fall asleep quickly after drinking, but your sleep can become less restorative, leaving you tired the next morning. Poor sleep caused by alcohol may lead to: Feeling tired after waking up Reduced concentration Lower mood Less energy during the day This does not mean you must completely avoid alcohol. However, keeping consumption moderate and avoiding drinking close to bedtime can help protect your sleep quality. If you notice that you regularly wake up feeling exhausted after summer evenings involving alcohol, reducing your intake may make a noticeable difference. 4. Longer Summer Days Can Disrupt Your Sleep Routine One of the best things about summer is the extra daylight. However, those longer evenings can also interfere with your body’s natural sleep rhythm. Your circadian rhythm is your internal clock that helps regulate when you feel awake and when you feel sleepy. Exposure to bright light late in the evening can delay the signals that tell your body it is time to rest. Early sunrises can also make it harder to sleep in, especially if your bedroom receives lots of morning sunlight. To improve summer sleep, consider: Using blackout curtains Wearing an eye mask Keeping your bedroom cool Following a consistent bedtime routine Reducing bright light exposure before sleep You do not need to avoid summer evenings completely, but creating a darker and calmer sleeping environment can help your body maintain a healthier rhythm. 5. Hay Fever Symptoms Can Make You More Tired For many people, summer means increased pollen levels and uncomfortable allergy symptoms. Hay fever can cause sneezing, itchy eyes, congestion, and difficulty breathing, all of which can interfere with sleep. A blocked nose can make it harder to breathe comfortably during the night. Poor-quality sleep caused by allergies may leave you feeling tired even if you spend enough hours in bed. Managing hay fever symptoms can help improve your sleep. Helpful strategies may include: Keeping windows closed when pollen levels are high Washing your face and hair after being outdoors Changing bedding regularly Using suitable allergy treatments recommended by healthcare professionals Some people also find nasal strips or saline nasal rinses helpful for improving airflow through the nose. How to Beat Summer Fatigue Naturally Feeling tired in summer does not always mean something is wrong. Often, your body is responding to changes in temperature, light exposure, routines, and lifestyle habits. Small adjustments can make a big difference. Stay hydrated, protect your sleep, manage allergies, avoid excessive alcohol, and take steps to stay cool during hot weather. If tiredness is severe, lasts for a long time, or affects your daily life, it is worth speaking to a healthcare professional to rule out other possible causes. Summer should be a season for enjoying life, not constantly fighting exhaustion. Understanding what causes summer fatigue can help you make simple changes and feel more energised throughout the warmer months. Source: The Independent (23 July 2026)e. Disclaimer: This article is for general informational purposes only and does not replace professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. If you have ongoing or unexplained fatigue, speak with a qualified healthcare professional. Individual health needs vary, and advice from a doctor or specialist should be followed where appropriate.

title: What Income Do You Need To Afford A $300k House?
summary: Explore what it may take to afford a $300K home, from income and down payment to monthly costs, and get helpful guidance for planning with Pennymac.
body_text: What Income Do You Need To Afford A $300k House? Learn what it takes to afford a $300,000 home, including the income you may need and how down payments, loan options and location influence your costs. July 29, 2026 min read Share In this article Tell me more! I'm looking to … Buy a Home Refinance My Loan Access Home Equity Earn cash back after close! With Home Connect, you could earn $350 to $9,500 cash back after close. Learn More Reading time: 7 minutes 18 seconds Many prospective buyers have their sights set on a $300,000 home. If that is your target housing price, the next thing to consider is how much income you need to afford it. It takes more than just looking at the mortgage amount. True affordability means balancing your monthly budget with the realities of the local market where you’re searching and the ongoing expenses of homeownership. Let’s break down what it takes to afford a $300,000 home so you can see how income, monthly payments and other costs come together. Understanding these factors can help you estimate what you may need to earn and where you stand as you start your search. Key takeaways: Most buyers need about $85,000 to $100,000 in annual income to afford a $300K home Your exact budget depends on debt, down payment, interest rates and local costs The 28/36 rule helps estimate how much of your income should go toward housing and total debt Monthly payments include more than the mortgage — think taxes, homeowners insurance and possibly mortgage insurance Two buyers with the same income may qualify for different loan amounts based on credit and financial profile Estimated Income Needed for a $300k House To afford a $300,000 home, most buyers need an annual income of roughly $85,000 to $100,000, depending on their debts, down payment and local costs. This range is based on common lending guidelines used to assess affordability. One guideline lenders use is the 28/36 rule. This rule helps determine how much of your income can reasonably be allocated to housing and total debt. Here’s what the 28/36 rule means: The “28” suggests keeping your housing payment at or below 28% of your gross monthly income. This payment includes your mortgage principal, interest, property taxes and homeowners insurance . The “36” suggests keeping your total debt at or below 36% of your gross monthly income. The number should take into account your housing payment, credit cards, student loans, car payments and any other loan obligations. These limits are used to calculate your debt-to-income (DTI) ratio . Your DTI is calculated by dividing your total monthly debt payments by your gross monthly income. For example, if you earn $7,500 per month and have $2,250 in total monthly debt, your DTI would be 30%. A lower DTI shows lenders that you have more room in your budget for a mortgage payment, which may improve your chances of approval. What does this mean for a $300,000 home? For a $300,000 home, applying these guidelines typically results in the $85,000 to $100,000 income range. Your specific number will depend on several variables, like your down payment amount, current interest rates and your local property tax rates. Using this income range as a starting point can help you understand how your finances align with a $300,000 home. What a Mortgage Payment for a $300k Home Might Look Like A mortgage refers to the loan amount you borrow to purchase a home, not the monthly payment itself. The total you borrow depends on your down payment. For example, putting 20% down on a $300,000 home means you contribute $60,000 upfront and borrow the remaining $240,000 as your mortgage. With a 3.5% down payment on a government-backed FHA loan , you would contribute $10,500 and borrow $289,500. These are just two examples. Your down payment can vary, and many buyers choose to put down more depending on their situation. But keep in mind that your monthly payment includes more than just repaying the amount you borrowed. It consists of several components. Lenders use the acronym PITI (Principal, Interest, Taxes and Insurance) to describe them: Principal: The portion that goes toward paying down your loan balance Interest: The cost of borrowing the money Taxes: Property taxes collected by your local government, often held in an escrow account Insurance: Homeowners insurance that protects your property against damage or liability Depending on your loan type and down payment, you may also pay mortgage insurance. This protects the lender if you are unable to make your payments. For conventional loans , mortgage insurance (PMI) is typically required if your down payment is less than 20% . It can be removed once you reach sufficient equity, usually when your loan balance drops to 80% of your home’s value or lower. FHA loans include mortgage insurance regardless of down payment. In many cases, this insurance remains for the life of the loan. To remove it, homeowners typically need to refinance from an FHA into a conventional loan once they have built enough equity and meet qualification requirements. Why Two Buyers With the Same Income Can Afford Very Different Homes While income provides a baseline for affordability, several other financial factors determine how much you can borrow. This is why two buyers earning the same salary might qualify for very different loan amounts. Here are some of the key factors that influence your borrowing power: Existing monthly debt : A buyer with high student loan payments, credit card balances or auto loans has less income available for a mortgage payment. This increases their debt-to-income (DTI) ratio and may limit how much they can borrow. Credit score : A higher credit score signals financial reliability to lenders and may help you qualify for a lower interest rate. A lower rate reduces your monthly payment and can increase the total home price you can afford. Down payment : A larger down payment reduces the amount you need to borrow. It can also lower your monthly payment and, in some cases, help you avoid mortgage insurance. Interest rates : Even a small variation in interest rates can significantly impact your monthly payment and overall affordability. Higher rates reduce how much home you can afford at the same income level. Property taxes, insurance and any applicable HOA fees : These costs vary by location and are included in your monthly housing payment. Higher taxes or insurance premiums can reduce your purchasing power. If the property is part of a homeowners association, you may also have HOA fees, which are paid separately. Real-Life Examples: What Affording a $300k Home Might Look Like To better understand how your down payment and loan type could affect your monthly budget, take a look at the following scenarios. They show how choices can change your costs. These estimates assume a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage at a 6.5% interest rate. Monthly payments include principal, interest and any applicable mortgage insurance. Scenario 1: 20% down with a conventional loan (no mortgage insurance) Home price: $300,000 Down payment: $60,000 Loan amount: $240,000 Estimated monthly payment (principal and interest): $1,515 to $1,550 Estimated income needed: $80,000 to $90,000 Scenario 2: 10% down with a conventional loan (with mortgage insurance) Home price: $300,000 Down payment: $30,000 Loan amount: $270,000 Estimated monthly payment (principal, interest and mortgage insurance): $1,850 to $1,900 Estimated income needed: $90,000 to $100,000 Scenario 3: 3.5% down with an FHA loan Home price: $300,000 Down payment: $10,500 Loan amount: $289,500 Estimated monthly payment (principal, interest and FHA mortgage insurance): $1,980 to $2,050 Estimated income needed: $95,000 to $105,000 These are illustrative examples only. This is not a promise of a specific rate or qualification but rather an example to help you visualize various monthly payments. Actual monthly payments will also include property taxes, homeowners insurance and HOA fees (if applicable). How Location Impacts What Income You’ll Need Geographic location influences how far a $300,000 budget will stretch. Property taxes, homeowners insurance premiums and local market conditions vary significantly from state to state and even by county and city. You will often find spacious single-family homes with yards for $300,000 in many parts of the Midwest and the South. Property taxes in these regions tend to be lower than in other parts of the country, leaving more of your budget for the home itself. Finding a single-family home at that price point may be less likely in expensive coastal markets like California or New York. You might need to adjust your search to include smaller condos, older properties or homes located further away from major city centers. Higher property taxes in some areas can also add hundreds of dollars to your monthly housing expenses. Ways to Make a $300k Home More Affordable You can take steps to make a $300,000 home more affordable and better aligned with your budget. Strengthen Your Credit Your credit score plays a key role in the rate and loan options available to you. Improving your score may help you qualify for better terms. Increase Your Down Payment A larger down payment reduces how much you need to borrow. Putting 20% down on a $300K home can also help you avoid mortgage insurance on a conventional loan. Compare Loan Options Different loan programs offer different advantages. FHA loans allow lower down payments and have more flexible credit requirements. VA loans , for eligible borrowers, may offer no down payment and no monthly mortgage insurance requirement. Exploring your options can help you find a loan that fits your situation. Apply With a Co-borrower Buying with a co-borrower allows you to combine incomes, which may improve your qualification and increase your purchasing power. It can also help you secure more favorable loan terms. Look Into Assistance Programs Homebuyer assistance programs may help with down payments or closing costs. These programs vary by location and eligibility, but they can reduce upfront expenses and make buying a home more manageable. What to Consider Before You Buy at This Price Point Buying a $300,000 home involves more than meeting a specific income target. While your income is a factor, you’ll also want to consider your ongoing expenses, savings and future plans — such as education, growing your family or preparing for retirement — to make sure your housing costs leave room for other priorities and goals. In addition to your down payment and monthly payment, you will need to plan for several upfront and ongoing costs, including: Closing costs: Typically range from 3% to 6% of the loan amount Cash reserves: Savings set aside after closing to handle unexpected costs Home expenses: Maintenance and repairs Once you understand how these costs fit into your budget, getting pre-approved for a mortgage can help you take the next step with confidence. During the pre-approval process, a lender reviews your income, credit and assets to estimate how much you may be able to borrow. Having a pre-approval helps define your budget and shows sellers that you are a qualified and serious buyer. Bottom Line: Income Is Just One Piece of the Puzzle Your salary is an important part of the home affordability equation, but it’s just one piece of the puzzle — no matter what price point you’re considering. Lenders look beyond income and evaluate your overall financial profile to determine a borrowing amount that fits your situation. You don’t have to figure this out on your own. Talk with a Pennymac Loan Expert who can help you weigh your options and find a path to homeownership that works with your budget. title: WeRide | WeRide Achieves Record Six Consecutive Wins at China Urban Intelligent Driving Competition
summary: WeRide (NASDAQ: WRD) is a leading global commercial-stage company that develops autonomous driving technologies from Level 2 to Level 4.
body_text: TIANJIN, China – June 14, 2026 – At the Tianjin event of the Second China Intelligent Driving Competition hosted by D1EV.COM, a leading electric and intelligent vehicle media platform, the Chery Exeed Sterra ES equipped with WeRide Driving (WRD 3.0), co-developed by WeRide and Bosch, took first place with its stable and efficient driving performance throughout the competition. This landmark victory secures the first and only six-win streak in the history of the competition , and further solidifies WRD 3.0's industry-leading position in consistent full-scene performance. Final results from the Second China Urban Intelligent Driving Competition (Tianjin round) Unlike previous sessions, the rules of Tianjin round introduced pivotal upgrades. For the first time, P2P NOA(Parking-to-Parking Navigation on ADAS) was incorporated into the scoring system, alongside evaluations of vehicles' full-journey driving performance in automatic parking exit, gate passage, complex public road navigation and automatic parking. Meanwhile, any parking failure or human takeover (including accelerator operation) results in score deductions. With tightened rules, the competition has evolved from a single evaluation of urban driving performance into a comprehensive evaluation of the overall continuity, stability and reliability of complete intelligent driving systems. Under the high-intensity assessment, WRD3.0 demonstrated outstanding systematic advantages with sustained top-tier performance across diverse driving scenarios. Unlike modular and two-stage driving solutions that suffer from data fragmentation and inconsistent decision-making strategies, WRD3.0 adopts a one-stage end-to-end large model to cover both driving and parking scenarios, enabling unified modeling and decision-making across diverse parking spaces. The system generates more precise and stable driving trajectories in low-speed parking scenarios. It also proficiently handles complex interactions with other vehicles, VRUs and various traffic participants in high-speed and intricate urban road conditions. The 2027 Exeed Sterra ES, equipped with the championship‑winning intelligent driving solution 2026 serves as a critical year for the large-scale commercial deployment of WRD 3.0. Hitherto, WRD 3.0 has secured mass-production design appointments for more than 30 vehicle types from Chery Automobile and GAC Group, with continuous expansion to more OEM customers and computing platforms. Moving forward, WeRide will continue to prioritize user experience. The company is committed to advance the technological iteration and deployment of WRD3.0, delivering user-friendly, reassuring and reliable advanced driving assistance experiences for consumers worldwide. About WeRide WeRide is a global leader and a first mover in the autonomous driving industry, as well as the first publicly traded Robotaxi company. Our autonomous vehicles have been deployed in over 40 cities across 12 countries. We are also the first and only technology company whose products have received autonomous driving permits in eight markets: China, the UAE, Singapore, France, Switzerland, Saudi Arabia, Belgium, and the US. Empowered by the smart, versatile, cost-effective, and highly adaptable WeRide One platform, WeRide provides autonomous driving products and services from L2 to L4, addressing transportation needs in the mobility, logistics, and sanitation industries. WeRide was named to Fortune's 2025 Change the World and 2025 Future 50 lists. title: Unlock the Power of ChatGPT for Video Security
summary: Explore potential use cases of ChatGPT, PaLM-2, and other LLMs for the Video Security Industry.
body_text: ChatGPT for the Video Security Industry In the rapidly evolving landscape of the connected world, businesses are constantly seeking innovative solutions that improve productivity and optimize user experiences. Artificial intelligence has already made waves in video surveillance and with technology continuously progressing is set to redefine the future of video surveillance.In this article, we will look into the potential applications and benefits of ChatGPT-4 in the realm of video surveillance. For years, Computer Vision (CV) and Deep Learning (DL) technologies have been the linchpins of AI in the video security domain. These breakthroughs paved the way for object detection, facial recognition, false alarm filtering, number plate recognition, and countless other products. By leveraging AI, traditional surveillance companies have reduced their reliance on human operators without compromising on security. What was once labor-intensive and prone to error has now been streamlined into an efficient and reliable process. The introduction of AI-driven systems based on Large Language Models (LLM) and its most notable representative, ChatGPT promises to start a new era of innovation. ‍ What is LLM and is ChatGPT the only name in town? With much buzz surrounding ChatGPT, it's essential to understand its capabilities and implications for the video security industry. LLMs are advanced machine learning models, specifically designed to understand, analyze, and generate human-like text. They can understand the nuances of languages and context, generate text and images, sound, and videos. One of the most popular LLM is GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer). Created by OpenAI, GPT-4 is the fourth iteration of this model that was designed to engage users in conversation and provide detailed responses based on text prompts. However, ChatGPT is not the sole contender in this arena. There are other large language models, such as Google's PaLM-2 , Meta’s LLaMA , Stanford’s Alpaca , and many more. These large language models are part of the rapidly growing field, were numerous companies and organizations developing their own models to tackle various language-related tasks. Stay tuned for our upcoming articles where we will explore and compare these models in detail. How ChatGPT and other LLMs can help in Video Surveillance The integration of LLMs into video surveillance systems offers numerous benefits, by automating labor-intensive tasks that were previously beyond the scope of Computer Vision. Here are just a few examples: Video Summarization: With ChatGPT, businesses can streamline their forensic video analysis by generating a concise summary, combining all finding into a single, easy-to-review text report. This report can be effortlessly stored, searched, or shared. Original videos remain accessible as source links, ensuring complacency and safeguarding the integrity of the investigative process. Intelligent Alerts: Utilizing its advanced language understanding capabilities, ChatGPT can parse complex security alerts and automatically generate intelligible incident reports. This helps security teams make informed, data-driven decisions and facilitates quick response times to potential threats. Contextual Analysis: ChatGPT can analyze the contextual information surrounding video content, offering insights into the environment, objects, and activities depicted in the footage. Ease of use: The LLM can seamlessly integrate with the company's access control management system, facilitating swift responses to a diverse range of inquiries related to physical access. visitor management, door reader analytics, and safety reporting. Here are some examples of the queries users can pose: "What is the current number of individuals present in the office?" "What is the total count of employees and visitors currently inside the shopping area" "How many new employee badges were issued last month?" "Display the list of cars that entered the parking lot last night." These are just a few sample queries that highlight the versatility and capabilities of such AI system. Addressing the Challenges of ChatGPT in Video Security While ChatGPT and other LLMs hold significant promise, deploying these technologies comes with inherent challenges and risks. One notable limitation is that LLMs do not directly handle video feeds on their own. As with any Natural Language Processing model(NLP), LLM relies on textual inputs. Therefore, leveraging videos requires the integration of a Computer Vision algorithm, such as the one developed by Traces AI. By combining the capabilities of ChatGPT and Traces AI's Computer Vision API, you can effectively communicate and extract valuable insights from video data. Another big challenge is " hallucination ", a phenomenon where the language model produces plausible-sounding but incorrect or nonsensical information. This poses a considerable obstacle when businesses' success relies on accurate and reliable information. Addressing and minimizing hallucinations is a crucial area of focus for AI professionals. We continually refine models, incorporating robust evaluation methodologies, and leverage human feedback, to mitigate hallucination and enhance the overall quality of responses. For businesses in the video security space, it is imperative to closely collaborate with AI experts when considering the implementation of LLMs. By partnering with professionals who possess expertise in both technology and video security, businesses can effectively leverage the advantages offered by LLMs while minimizing potential drawbacks. Traces boasts a remarkable team of professionals who have extensively tested the latest LLMs and have a proven track record in creating some of the most advanced AI video analytic systems. With our profound knowledge of Computer Vision and video security, we can determine the most suitable LLM for your specific business applications. Get in touch with us today to explore the possibilities of ChatGPT, PaLM, LLaMA, and many others. The Future of Video Security with LLM LLM holds immense potential for transforming the video security landscape, offering unprecedented capabilities in analyzing video data, streamlining processes, and fostering cross-functional collaboration. As the technology continues to mature, it's crucial for businesses to stay ahead of the curve and explore the possibilities that AI is unlocking.
